transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Patel (Redwood SE); Marta Ruiz (CTO - Atlas Finance); Devon Park (SRE); Sanjay Iyer (Product Lead); Leah Gomez (Security)

Auto-generated summary: (may be imperfect) Focus on go-live planning, canary, monitoring and compliance items.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: ok everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off, uh, quick agenda  recap pilot results, discuss rollout plan (canary/cutover), monitoring & runbooks, and next steps.
[00:12] Marta: Sounds good. Quick note, we're on a tight timeline, want to go live end of month if possible but first priority is safety and audit.
[00:20] Jordan: Understood. DevOps one of the key asks in last meeting was a dry-run for cutover, we built a canary plan  priya will walk through.
[00:28] Priya: hi team. Quick context  pilot has been running on Redwood Dedicated with quantized model variant, latency p95 at ~210ms, p99 sporadic spikes ~380ms on long prompts. Throughput looks stable. We recommend canary because it lets us validate routing, KV cash (sic) behavior and fallback policies.
[00:47] Devon: when you say p99 spikes, are those cold-starts or long-sequence artifacts?
[00:53] Priya: mostly long-sequence token growth and occasionally first-request for a warm pod after autoscale. We added prefix caching for top queries which reduced repeat latency by ~30%.
[01:04] Sanjay: any quality regressions with the quantized model? we noticed a few hallucinations in edge prompts during the last run.
[01:10] Priya: good callout; we ran evals on the top 200 prompts  objective metrics (BLEU-ish and human checks) show negligible degradation, but some prompts with heavy context show slight truncation; our recommended approach is to A/B test model variants during canary: 90/10 production/quantized for first 48 hours then expand.
[01:28] Marta: timeline wise, what's the canary cadence?
[01:31] Priya: propose: day 0 dry-run (no production traffic), day 1 canary at 5% for 24-48 hours; if metrics stable, ramp to 25% for 24 hours, then 50% and then full. We also recommend an immediate rollback policy if p99 latency >500ms for 15 minutes or error rate >1%.
[01:48] Devon: and error rate definition  5xx only or includes model-level failures?
[01:52] Jordan: we should track both. operational errors (5xx) and semantic failures (high divergence) mapped to user-reported quality. We'll have two alert buckets.
[02:02] Leah: on security, need confirmation on audit logs, SSO/SAML integration and KMS for key management. Can you confirm what logs Redwood retains during Dedicated vs Private?
[02:12] Priya: Dedicated includes request/response metadata logs, redaction can be enabled. For private deployments we hand off KMS keys; we support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated with HSM integration as an add-on. We'll ship the security whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts.
[02:28] Leah: ok please send the SOC2 doc and the KMS integration guide. Also we need encryption-in-transit details for cross-region traffic.
[02:36] Jordan: will do.
[02:39] [03:00]  pause  quick screen share references to canary playbook doc link (not pasted) 
[03:12] Priya: on monitoring  suggested thresholds: p95 latency alert at >300ms sustained for 10 minutes, p99 alert at >450ms for 5 minutes, error rate alert >1% for 5 minutes, and model-quality regressions (improvement/deterioration on sentinel prompt set) trigger a pager to SE & customer SRE. Also propose synthetic probing every 5 minutes for top 25 queries.
[03:40] Devon: synthetic probes are good. How do we compute quality regressions?
[03:44] Priya: we run lightweight heuristics plus occasional human review  divergence score and hallucination flags, and compare model outputs to baseline results; if >threshold we open a ticket and depending on severity auto-fallback to a higher-fidelity model.
[03:58] Sanjay: auto-fallback lanes mean higher cost  need to cap usage otherwise finance will freak.
[04:03] Jordan: agree, we'll set budget guardrails  e.g., fallback budget capped at X tokens per hour and notify product  and provide a dashboard to monitor spend in real-time.
[04:14] Marta: runbooks  who owns oncall during canary? Devon?
[04:18] Devon: yes Atlas SRE will own primary on-call, but Redwood will be second-level for model infra. We need a Slack channel and an agreed escalation path.
[04:27] Jordan: we'll set up a dedicated Slack channel and integrate with Redwood incident alerts. Priya will provide playbook steps: verify pod logs, check KV cache health, toggle model variant, rollback route to warm fallback.
[04:40] Priya: I'll attach the runbook sample after the call. It's a checklist: pre-checks, canary start, monitoring watch, rollback steps, postmortem template.
[04:50] Leah: audit and retention  Atlas requires 1 year of request metadata retention for compliance. Can Redwood support configurable retention and export to customer S3?
[04:59] Priya: yes, Dedicated supports configurable retention and log export to S3. For Private deployment we can do on-prem storage. We'll add that to the security doc.
[05:10] Jordan: ok signage: final approvals needed from Marta for go/no-go and from Leah for security. Proposed go-live window is 2026-05-20 to 2026-05-25; dry-run on 2026-05-12. Does that work?
[05:22] Marta: yes timeline looks doable, pending final security sign-off.
[05:26] Sanjay: small ask  can we do an A/B where 10% routed to Redwood and 90% to existing model to compare customer impact?
[05:33] Priya: absolutely  we can support a routing rule in the gateway, A/B metrics dashboard will include conversion and quality KPIs. A/B will take a bit longer to analyze, but useful.
[05:41] Devon: one more ops question  during rollout if autoscaler spins up new pods, any warmup latency we should expect?
[05:48] Priya: for Dedicated with pre-warmed pool, warmup is low; for large-seq requests there can still be KV cache coldness. We'll pre-warm based on historical top queries for canary.
[05:58] Jordan: let's recap actions  Jordan to send pricing & SLA, Priya to send playbook & runbook + canary template, Devon to confirm on-call coverage & Slack channel, Marta to approve guardrails and sign-off date. Any other items?
[06:12] Marta: please include the pilot regression query list  we'll send top 25 later today.
[06:18] Jordan: great. Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for dry-run and postmortem cadence.
[06:25] End meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (KV cash vs KV cache), speaker overlaps, and imperfect punctuation. References to docs: canary playbook (shared link), security whitepaper (will be emailed), pricing PDF (to follow).
